stem: What does this poster best show about how eastern audiences met the West in the 1890s?

stimulus.source_note: Buffalo Bill's Wild West poster, 1899 (Library of Congress, LCCN94513621). Public domain. Image viewed before writing.
stimulus.text: The poster advertises 'Buffalo Bill's Wild West and Congress of Rough Riders of the World,' 1899. At the right, Colonel W. F. Cody, 'Buffalo Bill,' sits on horseback, with the promise that he 'will appear at every performance.' The center shows 'Arab Horsemen' galloping and acrobats performing, and the banner at the bottom advertises 'the real Sons of the Soudan' and their feats of strength and horsemanship.

options.text: They learned the West from government reports and census bulletins
options.misconception: Background: census bulletins shaped Turner's essay, not a show poster; this poster sells tickets, not statistics.

options.text: They met it as a staged show of riders acting out feats
They met it by moving west in large numbers to homestead
options.misconception: Background: the poster sells seats to a show; its audience sat in eastern cities.

options.text: They learned it from Native leaders speaking in their own words
options.misconception: Background: Sitting Bull did tour with the show for a season, but the show staged him as an act, not as a speaker.

rationales.A: Background: census bulletins shaped Turner's essay, not a show poster. This poster sells tickets, not statistics.
rationales.B: The poster promises Cody himself at every performance, Arab horsemen, acrobats, and feats of strength. Background: the show toured the East from 1883, mythologizing the Old West just as the real Indian wars were ending.
rationales.C: Background: the poster sells seats to a show. Its audience sat in eastern cities.
rationales.D: Background: Sitting Bull did tour with the show for a season, but the show staged him as an act, not as a speaker.
rationales.general:
Picture a city crowd filing into a showground, expecting the West they have read about.
1. Read what the poster sells. Cody on horseback, rough riders of the world, feats of strength and horsemanship.
2. Ask what the crowd actually gets. A performance, staged and rehearsed, not the working West.
3. Name the meeting. The East met the West as a show.
Remember: a poster promises a thrill, not a history lesson, and the crowd pays for the thrill.

figures.alt: A colorful 1899 show poster. At the right, Buffalo Bill Cody sits on a horse in a fringed jacket and wide hat. The center shows Arab horsemen galloping, acrobats, and riders performing tricks, under the title Buffalo Bill's Wild West and Congress of Rough Riders of the World.
